label: Vault
desc: HashiCorp Vault for secrets, certificates, and encryption. On IKS/ROKS the clean path is External Secrets Operator, Vault Secrets Operator, and the Vault CSI provider. On VPC, Vault can run on VSIs and inject into instance workloads.
value: Stop stuffing cluster Secrets and VSI files with long-lived keys. ESO/VSO/CSI is the Kubernetes story; a Vault cluster on VPC is the VSI story.
questions: Is this secrets for IKS/ROKS (ESO, VSO, CSI) or for VPC VSIs?
Will they run Vault themselves on VPC, or consume IBM Cloud Secrets Manager instead?
Do they already have Consul or Terraform in the same HashiCorp stack?
differentiators: ESO, VSO, and CSI are documented Kubernetes injectors
Deployable on VPC VSIs next to the workloads
Same HashiCorp control plane as Terraform and Boundary

label: Boundary
desc: HashiCorp Boundary for identity-based access to VPC workloads without a jump host or client-to-site VPN.
value: When the conversation is 'how do admins SSH to VSIs', Boundary is the HashiCorp answer. Client-to-site VPN remains the IBM Cloud VPC answer.
questions: Do admins need SSH/RDP into VPC VSIs without a bastion?
Is this instead of, or in addition to, client-to-site VPN?
Will Vault issue the credentials Boundary brokers?
differentiators: No jump host on the VPC
Identity-aware sessions, not a network tunnel
Pairs with Vault for just-in-time credentials

label: IBM Verify
desc: IBM Security Verify family. Verify Access can run on the cluster as reverse proxy, runtime, and OIDC, including an operator in the Red Hat catalog on ROKS.
value: Cluster-native identity enforcement instead of only a SaaS login in front of the app. Pair with IBM Application Gateway when the front door should sit outside the app containers.
questions: Should Verify Access run as containers on IKS or ROKS?
Do they want the certified operator from the Red Hat catalog (ROKS)?
Is IBM Application Gateway the OIDC front door back to Verify instead?
differentiators: Verify Access ships as containers plus an OpenShift operator
Reverse proxy, runtime, and OIDC on the cluster
Works with IBM Application Gateway as an external OIDC front door

label: IBM Application Gateway
desc: Identity-aware reverse proxy that fronts cluster applications and does OIDC back to IBM Verify.
value: Put Verify in front of IKS/ROKS apps without rewriting the application. Gateway is the front door; Verify is the IdP.
questions: Should cluster apps get OIDC without code changes?
Is Verify already the IdP, or are they still on App ID / a custom IdP?
Does this sit in front of Ingress, or replace it?
differentiators: OIDC reverse proxy purpose-built for Verify
Fronts cluster apps without an app SDK
Pairs with Verify Access on the cluster

label: NS1 Connect
desc: Authoritative DNS and traffic steering. On IKS/ROKS, NS1 is an official ExternalDNS provider so Ingress and Route hostnames publish automatically. NS1 also has a Terraform provider. Across VPC and PowerVS regions, NS1 does global steering and failover.
value: One DNS control plane: ExternalDNS for cluster hostnames, Terraform for zones, and steering/failover for multi-region VPC and PowerVS front doors.
questions: Should Ingress and OpenShift Routes publish to NS1 via ExternalDNS?
Do they need global steering across multi-region VPC or PowerVS?
Is DNS still in CIS, or moving to NS1 Connect?
differentiators: Official ExternalDNS provider for Kubernetes and OpenShift Routes
First-class Terraform provider
Traffic steering and failover across IBM Cloud regions

label: SevOne
desc: Network performance and flow monitoring. Container metrics can land via Prometheus. SevOne is network and flow, not cluster operations. On VPC and PowerVS it can collect cloud flow logs along Direct Link / VPN → Transit Gateway → VPC and back.
value: The flow and network story next to Instana (apps) and IBM Cloud Monitoring (platform). Do not sell SevOne as the Kubernetes ops console.

Should cluster nodes scrape Prometheus into SevOne, or is that Instana?
Is this PowerVS plus VPC on the same Transit Gateway path?
differentiators: Cloud flow-log collection across DL, VPN, TGW, and VPC
Prometheus scrape for container node metrics
Explicitly not cluster ops — that stays Instana or IBM Cloud Monitoring
